fall.note: The 1905 code's grade across the sidewalk space: 'a uniform incline from the street line toward the curb line, with a fall of one inch in every three feet'. A city-wide rule eight months after the scene date, carried to 1 July 1904.

reveal.note: How far the curb's top stands above the roadway. No source read states it; the 1887-91 view and the owner's second photograph show a dressed stone curb about one stoop riser above the roadway, so 7 in.

section.road_note: The roadway's level below the field, everywhere: the fall across a 14-ft sidewalk space plus the reveal. On 50-ft 16th Street (a 10-ft space) the reveal comes out 1.3 in higher, so the two roadways meet level.

carriage_walks.note: One paved crossing of the parkway, walk to curb, at the middle of every lot at least 40 ft wide. The pictures show such crossings on these avenues (1815's, 2112's); which house had one, and where, is not recorded. The carriage blocks T-2474 stood beside them were withdrawn by T-3198: no picture shows one.

carriage_posts.note: Stone posts at the curb, only where a picture shows them; each varied by its own seed. Square with a domed cap (1815) or round-topped and painted white (the 2100 block).

corner_crossings.note: At every corner each face's walk is carried on across the other street's parkway and over the curb, and from the curb's face one dressed stone slab slopes out and down onto the roadway. Pictured at the Glessner and Pullman corners of 18th and Prairie; elsewhere by that rule.

crossings.note: The Glessner corner: two stone slabs slope from the curb's top to the roadway, one each way across, the lamp's stone footing between them.
The Pullman corner: the walks carried across the parkway either side of a curbed grass corner with the lamp, down to the roadway at the curb.
